title: oa-responses-interop-unified-event-contract-loss-detection
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create a compact, testable compatibility layer that maps Redwood's streaming + function-call model to OpenAI Responses semantics with an explicit unified event contract and a lossiness detection score. This ticket covers design and an initial runtime prototype for a gateway that performs event normalization, maps function/tool-call lifecycle events, and computes an observable "loss_score" when deterministic mapping is lossy. The aim is to reduce customer regressions during openai-responses migrations and provide clear telemetry + remediation guidance.
background: Multiple recent migrations surfaced edge cases where streaming boundaries, interim 'tool_start'/'tool_end' events, and structured output envelopes diverge between Redwood's runtime and OpenAI Responses. Those mismatches caused tool invocation order flips, truncated structured outputs, and opaque degradation that customers observed as behavior changes. Existing compatibility tickets catalog gaps but lack a single contract and scoring mechanism for triage.
proposed_solution: Design and implement a lightweight compatibility gateway that sits between the API layer and the runtime. Key components: 1) Unified Event Contract (UEC) that canonicalizes streaming chunks, function/tool events, and structured output frames into a small event set (INIT, TOKEN, TOOL_CALL_START, TOOL_CALL_STEP, TOOL_CALL_END, STRUCT_FRAME, DONE). 2) Lossiness Detector: deterministic rules + heuristics that produce a loss_score 0-100 with categories (schema_loss, ordering_loss, truncation, type_mismatch). 3) Schema Canonicalizer: mapping rules to translate OpenAI-structured-outputs to Redwood's expected JSON schema with backoff/repair operations. 4) Canary mode that emits enriched telemetry (event diffs, loss_score) and optional synthetic replay to verify semantics. Provide runtime flags to enable strict vs best-effort modes and a developer-facing report for post-migration auditing.
acceptance_criteria: UEC documented with examples for streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs
Prototype gateway implements canonicalization and outputs loss_score per request
End-to-end test harness that replays 500 recorded OpenAI Responses sessions and asserts loss_score < 10 for 85% of baseline workloads
Telemetry dashboard tile showing loss_score distribution and top loss reasons
Playbook for remediation when loss_score >= 50 including suggested runtime flags and operator steps
technical_notes: UEC must preserve token-level offsets for prefix-caching reuse in Redwood runtime
Lossiness rules: missing TOOL_CALL_END => truncation; re-ordered TOOL_CALL_START events => ordering_loss; STRUCT_FRAME type mismatch => schema_loss
Gateway should be implemented as a sidecar/proxy in the API pod to keep experimental outage blast radius low
Performance goal: added median latency < 6ms at 95th percentile for small requests; bulk streaming benchmark required before enabling by default
Use existing telemetry pipeline (metrics + logs + traces) and add a new 'responses.compat.loss_score' metric with tags: reason, model, customer_tier
risks: Incorrect canonicalization could introduce semantic regressions for important customer tool workflows
High cardinality telemetry could add cost and noise; need sampling and aggregation rules
Runtime-sidecar approach may complicate Dedicated/Private deployment installs — ops coordination required
decisions: Use sidecar gateway in API tier instead of monolithic runtime patch to limit scope and enable rapid rollback (decision 2026-02-27)
Loss_score will be an integer 0-100 derived from weighted rule outcomes; thresholds aligned with QA team (low < 10, medium 10-49, high >= 50)
Initial canonicalization will target the 80% common patterns; rare edge cases will be surfaced via telemetry and mapped in followups
